subject: Chemistry
text: (a) Write the molecular formula of the following carbon compounds: (i) Methane (ii) Propane. (b) Carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points. Why? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Methane: CH4; Propane: C3H8. (b) Most carbon compounds are covalent (molecular) compounds, so the intermolecular forces of attraction between their molecules are weak (van der Waals forces), not strong forces like in ionic compounds. Only a small amount of energy is needed to overcome these weak forces, so carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points.
keyPoints: Methane = CH4, Propane = C3H8
Carbon compounds are largely covalent/molecular, not ionic
Weak intermolecular (van der Waals) forces need little energy to break

subject: Chemistry
text: The electrons in the atoms of two elements X and Y are distributed in three shells having 1 and 7 electrons respectively in their outermost shells. (a) Write the group numbers of these elements in the Modern Periodic Table. (b) Write the molecular formula of the compound formed when X and Y combine with each other. (c) Which of the two is electropositive? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: X has configuration 2,8,1 (atomic number 11, sodium) so it belongs to Group 1. Y has configuration 2,8,7 (atomic number 17, chlorine) so it belongs to Group 17. (b) X and Y combine by transfer of the one outer electron of X to Y, forming the ionic compound NaCl. (c) X (sodium) is electropositive since it loses an electron to form a positive ion.
keyPoints: Configuration 2,8,1 → Group 1; configuration 2,8,7 → Group 17
Compound formed: NaCl
X (the Group 1 element) is electropositive

subject: Biology
text: (a) Which of the following flowers will have higher possibility of self-pollination? Mustard, Papaya, Watermelon, Hibiscus. (b) List the two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Mustard, because it is a bisexual flower in which the anther and stigma are close together and mature around the same time, favouring self-pollination; Papaya and Watermelon have unisexual flowers (separate male and female flowers), so they cannot self-pollinate. (b) The two reproductive parts of a bisexual flower are the stamen (androecium, the male part that produces pollen) and the pistil/carpel (gynoecium, the female part containing the ovary, style and stigma).
keyPoints: Mustard is bisexual with anther and stigma close together — self-pollination possible
Papaya and Watermelon are unisexual, so self-pollination is not possible
Reproductive parts: stamen (male) and pistil/carpel (female)

subject: Biology
text: Which one of the two multicellular organisms, Spirogyra and Planaria, reproduces by regeneration and why? Give an example of any other organism which can also reproduce by the same process. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Planaria reproduces by regeneration: if its body is cut into pieces, each piece contains cells that can divide repeatedly and differentiate into all the different cell types needed, so each piece grows into a complete new organism. (Spirogyra instead reproduces by fragmentation, simply breaking into pieces that each grow, without this specialised regenerative process.) Hydra is another organism that reproduces by regeneration.
keyPoints: Planaria reproduces by regeneration
Cells in the body fragment divide and differentiate to rebuild the whole organism
Another example: Hydra

subject: Biology
text: What is variation? List two main reasons that may lead to variation in a population. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Variation is the difference in characters/traits seen among individuals of the same species/population. Two main reasons for variation: (i) inaccuracies (mutations) that occur while copying DNA during reproduction; (ii) in sexual reproduction, DNA from two parents combines and reshuffles (recombination), producing offspring with new combinations of traits.
keyPoints: Variation = differences in traits among individuals of a population
Reason 1: errors/mutations during DNA copying
Reason 2: recombination of DNA from two parents in sexual reproduction

subject: Physics
text: (a) Name and state the rule that determines the direction of force experienced by a current-carrying straight conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field which is perpendicular to it. (b) An alpha particle, while passing through a magnetic field, gets deflected towards north. In which direction will an electron be deflected when it passes through the same magnetic field? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other; if the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor. (b) An alpha particle is positively charged and an electron is negatively charged, so the force on the electron in the same field (moving the same way) is in the opposite direction — the electron will be deflected towards the south.
keyPoints: Rule: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Thumb = force, forefinger = field, middle finger = current
Opposite charge (electron vs alpha particle) means the deflection is reversed — south

subject: Biology
text: What is ozone? How is it formed in the upper layers of the atmosphere? How does ozone affect our ecosystem? (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: Ozone (O3) is a molecule made of three oxygen atoms. In the upper atmosphere (stratosphere), high-energy ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun splits some oxygen molecules (O2) into free oxygen atoms, which then combine with other O2 molecules to form ozone (O3). The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful UV radiation from the sun, shielding living organisms on Earth from its damaging effects (such as skin cancer and damage to DNA), so it protects the ecosystem.
keyPoints: Ozone = O3, three oxygen atoms
Formed when UV radiation splits O2 into O atoms, which combine with O2 to form O3
Ozone layer absorbs harmful UV radiation, protecting living organisms

subject: Chemistry
text: (a) List two advantages of adopting the atomic number of an element as the basis of classifying elements in the Modern Periodic Table. (b) Write the electronic configurations of the elements X (atomic number 13) and Y (atomic number 20). (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Two advantages: (i) Classifying by atomic number correctly explains the periodicity of properties, since elements with the same number of valence electrons (which atomic number determines) recur periodically — this fixed anomalies of Mendeleev's atomic-mass-based table, such as the correct ordering of pairs like cobalt-nickel or argon-potassium. (ii) Atomic number equals the number of protons/electrons, which directly determines an element's electronic configuration and hence its chemical properties, making the classification more scientifically sound and predictive. (b) X (atomic number 13): electronic configuration 2, 8, 3 (aluminium). Y (atomic number 20): electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 2 (calcium).
keyPoints: Atomic number fixes anomalies like Co-Ni, Ar-K ordering seen with atomic mass
Atomic number = number of electrons, which fixes electronic configuration and properties

subject: Chemistry
text: Draw two different possible structures of a saturated hydrocarbon having four carbon atoms in its molecule. What are these two structures of the hydrocarbon having the same molecular formula called? Write the molecular formula and the common name of this compound. Also write the molecular formula of its alkyne. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: The saturated hydrocarbon with four carbon atoms is butane, C4H10. Its two structures are: n-butane, a straight chain, CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3; and isobutane (2-methylpropane), a branched chain, CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3. Structures with the same molecular formula but different arrangements of atoms are called isomers (chain isomers). Molecular formula: C4H10; common name: butane. The corresponding alkyne (butyne) has molecular formula C4H6.
keyPoints: Straight-chain n-butane: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3; branched isobutane: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3
Same molecular formula, different structure → called isomers
Molecular formula C4H10, common name butane; its alkyne (butyne) is C4H6

subject: Biology
text: (a) Mention one function each of the following organs in the human male reproductive system: (i) Testis (ii) Scrotum (iii) Vas deferens (iv) Prostate gland. (b) Name the type of germ cell which (i) is motile, and (ii) stores food. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) (i) Testis: produces sperm (male gametes) and the hormone testosterone. (ii) Scrotum: a pouch that keeps the testes outside the abdominal cavity at a lower temperature suitable for sperm production. (iii) Vas deferens: carries sperm from the testis to the urethra. (iv) Prostate gland: secretes fluid that, along with secretions of other glands, forms the seminal fluid that nourishes and helps transport sperm. (b) (i) The sperm (male gamete) is motile, using its tail to swim. (ii) The ovum/egg (female gamete) stores food (nutrients) for the early development of the embryo.
keyPoints: Testis: produces sperm and testosterone; scrotum: keeps testes cool; vas deferens: carries sperm; prostate: adds seminal fluid
Motile germ cell: sperm
Food-storing germ cell: ovum/egg

subject: Physics
text: (a) Define electric power and write its SI unit. (b) Two bulbs rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to an electric mains of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the bulbs from the mains. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (or work is done) in a circuit: P = W/t = VI = I²R = V²/R. Its SI unit is the watt (W). (b) In parallel, both bulbs get the full mains voltage of 220 V, so together they consume 100 W + 60 W = 160 W. Total current drawn = P/V = 160/220 ≈ 0.73 A.
keyPoints: Electric power = rate of consumption of electrical energy; P = VI; SI unit is watt
In parallel, total power = sum of individual powers = 160 W
Current from mains = P/V = 160/220 ≈ 0.73 A

subject: Biology
text: (a) Name the group of organisms which form the first trophic level of all food chains. Why are they called so? (b) Why are human beings most adversely affected by bio-magnification? (c) State one ill-effect of the absence of decomposers from a natural ecosystem. (2022 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Producers (autotrophs, e.g. green plants) form the first trophic level, because they make their own food through photosynthesis and so are the ultimate source of energy for every food chain. (b) Humans are most adversely affected by bio-magnification because they usually occupy the topmost trophic level in food chains, so harmful chemicals (like pesticides) that increase in concentration at each successive trophic level reach their highest concentration by the time they reach humans. (c) Without decomposers, dead remains and waste would not be broken down, so nutrients would never be recycled back into the soil/ecosystem, disrupting the nutrient cycle.
keyPoints: Producers are the first trophic level — they make their own food via photosynthesis
Humans are at the top of most food chains, so bio-magnified toxins reach their highest concentration in humans
Without decomposers, dead matter piles up and nutrients are not recycled

subject: Biology
text: What is the function of the diaphragm in the human respiratory system? Where is it present in the human body? (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle that helps change the volume of the chest (thoracic) cavity during breathing: it contracts and flattens during inhalation, expanding the chest cavity so air is drawn into the lungs, and it relaxes and domes upward during exhalation, pushing air out. It is present at the base of the thoracic (chest) cavity, separating it from the abdominal cavity.
keyPoints: Diaphragm changes the volume of the chest cavity to draw air in/push air out
Contracts and flattens during inhalation; relaxes/domes up during exhalation
Located at the base of the chest cavity, between chest and abdomen

subject: Biology
text: State two differences between the act of chewing food and salivation on sight of food. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Chewing is a voluntary, mechanical action — consciously controlled by the jaw muscles to physically break food into smaller pieces. Salivation on sight of food is an involuntary reflex action — it is triggered automatically by the brain/nervous system (even before food is in the mouth) and results in the chemical secretion of saliva by the salivary glands, not a mechanical breakdown.
keyPoints: Chewing = voluntary, mechanical breakdown of food by jaw muscles/teeth
Salivation on sight of food = involuntary reflex, triggered by the brain before food is even eaten
One is a physical action, the other is a glandular secretion response

subject: Biology
text: OR: State two differences between pollination and fertilization. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower, an external process occurring on the flower itself. Fertilization is the fusion of the male gamete (carried down the pollen tube) with the female gamete (egg cell) inside the ovule, an internal process that happens within the ovary, and it can only occur after pollination has taken place.
keyPoints: Pollination: transfer of pollen from anther to stigma (external, on the flower)
Fertilization: fusion of male and female gametes inside the ovule (internal, in the ovary)
Fertilization always occurs after pollination

subject: Biology
text: Given below is a pyramid showing various trophic levels in an ecosystem: (i) Producers (ii) Primary consumers (iii) Secondary consumers (iv) Tertiary consumers. (a) From the organisms listed below, identify which one is to be placed at which trophic level: Deer, Grass, Lion, Snake, Rabbit. (b) Discuss the reason why primary consumers will have more energy as compared to secondary consumers. (c) Why is the base of the pyramid broad? (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Grass — producer (level i); Deer and Rabbit — primary consumers (level ii, herbivores that eat grass); Snake — secondary consumer (level iii, eats primary consumers like the rabbit); Lion — tertiary consumer (level iv, apex predator). (b) At each trophic level only about 10% of the energy is passed on to the next level (the rest is lost as heat, used in respiration, or in body parts not eaten); since primary consumers are one level below secondary consumers, they retain more of the original energy captured by producers. (c) The base of the pyramid is broad because producers have the greatest energy/biomass/numbers, and both energy and numbers decrease sharply at each successive trophic level (only about 10% is transferred upward), so the pyramid narrows towards the top.
keyPoints: Grass = producer; Deer & Rabbit = primary consumers; Snake = secondary consumer; Lion = tertiary consumer
Only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level, so primary consumers retain more energy than secondary consumers
Base is broad because producers have the most energy/biomass, which shrinks at each higher level

subject: Biology
text: Give differences between the following: (a) Nephron and neuron (b) Sensory nerve and motor nerve (c) Consumers and decomposers. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) A nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney, responsible for filtering blood and forming urine (part of the excretory system); a neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, responsible for conducting electrical nerve impulses. (b) Sensory nerves carry impulses from sense organs/receptors to the brain or spinal cord (afferent); motor nerves carry impulses from the brain or spinal cord to muscles or glands (efferent). (c) Consumers depend on other organisms (producers or other consumers) for food and obtain organic matter directly; decomposers break down dead and decaying organic matter into simpler substances, releasing nutrients back into the environment.
keyPoints: Nephron = unit of the kidney (excretion); neuron = unit of the nervous system (impulse conduction)
Sensory nerves carry impulses TO the brain/spinal cord; motor nerves carry impulses FROM them
Consumers eat other organisms for food; decomposers break down dead matter and recycle nutrients

subject: Chemistry
text: Give reasons for the following: (a) Covalent compounds are poor conductors of electricity. (b) Soap does not form lather in hard water. (c) Carbon shows catenation but silicon does not. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Covalent compounds do not form ions — their molecules are electrically neutral, with electrons tightly shared between the bonded atoms, so there are no free-moving charged particles (ions or free electrons) to carry an electric current. (b) Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium salts (Ca2+, Mg2+ ions); these ions react with soap to form an insoluble precipitate (scum), so the soap gets used up in this reaction instead of producing lather. (c) Carbon atoms are small, forming strong and stable C-C bonds, which allows carbon to link with itself extensively (catenation); silicon atoms are larger, so Si-Si bonds are much weaker and less stable, so silicon shows very limited catenation.
keyPoints: Covalent compounds have no free ions/electrons to carry current
Ca2+/Mg2+ in hard water react with soap to form insoluble scum instead of lather
Small carbon atoms form strong stable C-C bonds (catenation); silicon's larger atoms form weak Si-Si bonds

subject: Chemistry
text: Write chemical equations for the following: (a) Oxidation of ethanol by acidified K2Cr2O7. (b) Hydrogenation of ethene. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) CH3CH2OH + 2[O] --(acidified K2Cr2O7, heat)--> CH3COOH + H2O (ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid). (b) CH2=CH2 + H2 --(Ni catalyst)--> CH3-CH3 (ethene is hydrogenated to ethane).
keyPoints: Ethanol + acidified K2Cr2O7 (oxidising agent) → ethanoic acid (acetic acid) + water
Ethene + H2 in presence of Ni catalyst → ethane
Both are examples of addition/oxidation reactions in carbon compounds

subject: Physics
text: The resistance of a wire of radius 0.01 cm and length 1.0 cm is 7 Ω. Calculate its resistivity. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: Radius r = 0.01 cm = 1 x 10⁻⁴ m, so cross-section area A = πr² = π x (1 x 10⁻⁴)² ≈ 3.14 x 10⁻⁸ m². Length L = 1.0 cm = 1 x 10⁻² m. Using R = ρL/A, resistivity ρ = RA/L = (7 x 3.14 x 10⁻⁸) / (1 x 10⁻²) ≈ 2.2 x 10⁻⁵ Ω m.
keyPoints: Convert radius and length to metres, find area A = πr²
Use R = ρL/A, rearranged to ρ = RA/L
Resistivity ≈ 2.2 x 10⁻⁵ Ω m

subject: Physics
text: OR: An electric heater is rated 220 V; 11 A. Calculate the power consumed if the heater is operated at 200 V. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: The heater's resistance (assumed constant) is R = V/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω. When operated at 200 V, power consumed P = V²/R = 200²/20 = 40000/20 = 2000 W.
keyPoints: Find resistance from rated values: R = V/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω
Resistance stays the same when the operating voltage changes
Power at 200 V: P = V²/R = 200²/20 = 2000 W

subject: Physics
text: The pattern of magnetic field due to a current-carrying wire depends upon the shape made by that wire. Justify. (2026 Board)
modelAnswer: A straight current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field in the form of concentric circles around it (direction given by the right-hand thumb rule). When the wire is bent into a circular loop, the field contributions from all parts of the loop add up (superpose); near the centre of the loop they all point the same way, so the field there is nearly straight and stronger than around a straight wire. In a solenoid (many circular turns of wire), the fields of all the turns add up along the axis, producing a strong, uniform field inside that resembles the field of a bar magnet. Since the field at any point is the combined effect of the current in every part of the wire, changing the wire's shape changes how those contributions add up, so the overall field pattern depends on the shape of the conductor.
keyPoints: Straight wire: concentric circular field lines around it
Circular loop: field contributions add up, becoming nearly straight/uniform near the centre
Solenoid: fields of many loops add along the axis, giving a strong uniform field like a bar magnet

subject: Chemistry
text: When magnesium ribbon is burnt in air, an ash of white colour is produced. Write chemical equation for the reaction giving the chemical name of the ash produced. State the type of chemical reaction giving justification for your answer. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. The white ash is magnesium oxide. This is a combination reaction (and also an oxidation reaction) — two substances (magnesium and oxygen) combine to form a single new substance, magnesium oxide.
keyPoints: Balanced equation: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO
White ash = magnesium oxide (MgO)
Combination reaction: two reactants combine to form one product

subject: Biology
text: Where are auxins synthesized? How do they promote phototropism? (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: Auxins are synthesized at the tip of the stem (shoot tip). During phototropism, auxin accumulates in greater concentration on the shaded side of the shoot (away from light); this causes cells on that side to elongate faster than on the illuminated side, so the shoot bends towards the light source.
keyPoints: Auxins are synthesized at the shoot tip
They accumulate more on the shaded side of the shoot
Faster cell elongation on the shaded side bends the shoot towards light

subject: Biology
text: List any two pairs of visible contrasting characters of garden pea plants used by Mendel for his experiments, stating the dominant and recessive characters in each pair. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: Two examples: (1) Stem height — Tall (dominant) vs Dwarf (recessive). (2) Seed shape — Round (dominant) vs Wrinkled (recessive). (Other valid pairs: seed colour — yellow (dominant) vs green (recessive); flower colour — violet (dominant) vs white (recessive).)
keyPoints: Stem height: Tall (dominant) vs Dwarf (recessive)
Seed shape: Round (dominant) vs Wrinkled (recessive)
Other valid pairs: seed colour (yellow/green), flower colour (violet/white)

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: When do we say that a particular person is suffering from hypermetropia? List two causes of this defect. Name the type of lens used to correct this defect. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: A person has hypermetropia (long-sightedness) when they can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects clearly, because the image of a close object forms behind the retina. Two causes: (i) the eyeball has become too short, or (ii) the focal length of the eye lens has increased (its curvature/power has decreased) too much. It is corrected using a convex (converging) lens.
keyPoints: Hypermetropia: distant objects clear, near objects blurred (image forms behind the retina)
Causes: eyeball too short, or eye lens's focal length too long/power too low
Corrected with a convex (converging) lens

subject: Biology
text: What are decomposers? List two consequences of their absence in an ecosystem. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: Decomposers are organisms (bacteria and fungi) that break down dead and decaying organic matter into simpler substances. Two consequences of their absence: (i) dead remains and waste would keep accumulating instead of being broken down; (ii) nutrients would not be recycled back into the soil/ecosystem, disrupting the nutrient cycle for producers.
keyPoints: Decomposers = bacteria and fungi that break down dead/decaying matter
Without them, dead matter and waste would keep piling up
Nutrients would not be recycled back into the soil, disrupting the nutrient cycle

subject: Chemistry
text: State reasons for the following: (a) Zinc oxide is an amphoteric oxide. (b) Sodium metal is stored in bottle filled with kerosene oil. (c) In the reactions of nitric acid with metals, generally hydrogen gas is not evolved. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Zinc oxide reacts with both acids and bases to form salt and water (behaving as a base with acids, and as an acid with bases), so it is amphoteric. (b) Sodium is a highly reactive metal that reacts vigorously with oxygen and moisture in air (can even catch fire); storing it under kerosene oil keeps it away from air. (c) Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent — it oxidises the hydrogen produced in the reaction with a metal to water, so hydrogen gas is generally not observed (except with very dilute nitric acid reacting with metals like Mg or Mn).
keyPoints: ZnO reacts with both acids and bases (behaves as both a base and an acid) — amphoteric
Sodium is highly reactive with air/moisture, so it's stored under kerosene to keep it away from air
Nitric acid oxidises the hydrogen produced into water instead of releasing H2 gas

subject: Chemistry
text: State giving reason the reduction process to obtain the following metals from their compounds: (i) Mercury, (ii) Copper and (iii) Sodium. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Mercury: a moderately reactive metal, obtained by simply heating its sulphide ore (cinnabar, HgS) in air — the oxide formed decomposes further on heating to give the metal directly (self-reduction). (ii) Copper: similarly moderately reactive; obtained by roasting its sulphide ore and reduction (self-reduction of Cu2S on heating in air). (iii) Sodium: a highly reactive metal that cannot be reduced by carbon; obtained by electrolytic reduction of its molten chloride (electrolysis of molten NaCl).
keyPoints: Mercury: moderately reactive, obtained by heating its sulphide ore in air (self-reduction)
Copper: similarly moderately reactive, obtained by roasting/self-reduction of its sulphide ore
Sodium: highly reactive, obtained by electrolytic reduction of molten sodium chloride

subject: Chemistry
text: OR: State giving reason for the change in appearance observed when each of the following metal is exposed to atmospheric air for some time: (i) Silver, (ii) Copper and (iii) Iron. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Silver turns black/tarnishes because it reacts with sulphur compounds (like H2S) in the air, forming a layer of silver sulphide. (ii) Copper develops a dull green coating because it reacts with moist carbon dioxide/moisture in air, forming basic copper carbonate on its surface. (iii) Iron develops a reddish-brown coating (rust — hydrated iron oxide) because it reacts with oxygen and moisture in air (rusting).
keyPoints: Silver tarnishes black due to reaction with sulphur compounds (H2S) in air, forming silver sulphide
Copper turns dull green due to reaction with moist CO2, forming basic copper carbonate
Iron rusts (reddish-brown hydrated iron oxide) due to reaction with oxygen and moisture

subject: Biology
text: We water the soil but it reaches the topmost leaves of the plants. Explain in brief the process involved. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: Water absorbed by root hairs from the soil moves up through the plant's xylem vessels. Continuous loss of water vapour from the leaf surfaces (transpiration, through stomata) creates a suction/pull that draws water upward through the xylem, forming a continuous column that is pulled all the way up to the topmost leaves — this is called the transpiration pull.
keyPoints: Root hairs absorb water from the soil into the xylem
Transpiration (water vapour loss through leaf stomata) creates a pulling force
This transpiration pull draws the water column upward through the xylem to the topmost leaves

subject: Biology
text: (a) List two constituents of Central Nervous System (CNS). How are these components protected from injuries? (b) Write two limitations of the use of electrical impulses. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) The two constituents of the CNS are the brain and the spinal cord. The brain is protected by the skull (a bony box), and the spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column (backbone) — both are further cushioned by cerebrospinal fluid and protective membranes. (b) Two limitations of electrical (nerve) impulses: (i) they can only reach cells connected by neurons, so they cannot control cells with no nervous connection; (ii) once used, a nerve impulse cannot easily be sustained for a prolonged/lasting effect, so the body relies on hormones (not just nerve impulses) for long-term or widespread regulation.
keyPoints: CNS constituents: brain (protected by the skull) and spinal cord (protected by the vertebral column)
Nerve impulses can only act on cells connected via neurons
Electrical impulses can't easily sustain a long-lasting effect, so hormones are needed for that

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: Name and explain the phenomenon of light due to which the path of a beam of light becomes visible when it enters a smoke filled room through a small hole. Also state the dependence of colour of the light we receive on the size of the particle of the medium through which the beam of light passes. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: This is the Tyndall effect — the scattering of light by particles suspended in its path (like smoke particles), which makes the path of the beam visible. The colour of the scattered light depends on the size of the scattering particles: smaller particles scatter shorter wavelengths (blue light) more strongly, while larger particles scatter longer wavelengths (or scatter all colours more uniformly, appearing whitish).
keyPoints: This is the Tyndall effect: light scattered by suspended particles, making the beam's path visible
Smaller particles scatter shorter (blue) wavelengths more
Larger particles scatter longer wavelengths, or scatter all colours more evenly (appearing white)

subject: Physics
text: Explain in brief the function of an electric fuse in a domestic circuit. An electric heater of current rating 3 kW; 220 V is to be operated in an electric circuit of rating 5 A. What is likely to happen when the heater is switched 'ON'? Justify your answer with necessary calculation. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: An electric fuse is a safety device connected in series in a circuit; it melts and breaks the circuit if the current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the wiring/appliances from damage due to overheating or short-circuits. The heater draws current I = P/V = 3000/220 ≈ 13.6 A, which far exceeds the circuit's safe rating of 5 A. So when switched ON, the fuse in the 5 A circuit would blow (melt) and disconnect the circuit — the heater cannot safely be operated on this circuit.
keyPoints: Fuse melts and breaks the circuit if current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the circuit
Heater's current draw = P/V = 3000/220 ≈ 13.6 A
13.6 A far exceeds the circuit's 5 A rating, so the fuse would blow when switched on

subject: Physics
text: (a) State Ohm's law. Write formula for the equivalent resistance Rp of the parallel combination of three resistors of values R1, R2 and R3. (b) Find the resistance of the following network of resistors: a resistor R in series (from X), leading into two resistors of value R connected in parallel with each other, continuing on to Y. (2024 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Ohm's law: at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends (V = IR, with R constant). For resistors in parallel: 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3. (b) The two parallel resistors (each R) combine to R/2. This is in series with the first R, so total resistance from X to Y = R + R/2 = 3R/2.
keyPoints: Ohm's law: V = IR (current ∝ potential difference, at constant temperature)
Parallel resistors: 1/Rp = 1/R1+1/R2+1/R3
Network: two parallel R's give R/2, in series with the first R gives 3R/2 total

subject: Biology
text: Besides minimising the loss of blood, why is it essential to plug any leak in a blood vessel? Name the component of blood which helps in this process and state how this component performs this function. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: It is essential to plug a leak because, besides preventing blood loss, an open wound is also an entry point for germs/infections into the body. Platelets are the blood component that helps in this process — at the site of injury, platelets clump together and help clot the blood, forming a plug that seals the wound.
keyPoints: Plugging a leak prevents blood loss and also blocks entry of germs/infection
Platelets are the component responsible
Platelets clump together at the wound site to clot the blood and seal it

subject: Biology
text: OR: (i) The transport system in plants is relatively slower than in animals. Give reasons. (ii) State the role of phloem in the transport of materials in plants. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Plant transport is slower because plants don't need to move materials as quickly as animals — they have lower energy demands (no locomotion), and transport through xylem/phloem tissues happens by relatively slow processes (like diffusion, transpiration pull, and pressure-driven flow) rather than a pumped circulatory system. (ii) Phloem transports food (organic nutrients made during photosynthesis, mainly sucrose) from the leaves to all other parts of the plant, including storage organs and growing regions — this process is called translocation, and can move materials in both upward and downward directions using energy from ATP.
keyPoints: Plants have lower energy demands (no locomotion) so slower transport suffices
Plant transport relies on diffusion/pressure-driven flow rather than a pumped circulatory system
Phloem carries out translocation — transport of food (sucrose) from leaves to the rest of the plant, using energy

subject: Physics
text: An object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Use the lens formula to find the position of the image formed in this case. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: For a concave lens, f = −30 cm, u = −60 cm. Lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/(−30) + 1/(−60) = −2/60 − 1/60 = −3/60 = −1/20. So v = −20 cm. The image forms 20 cm from the lens, on the same side as the object (virtual image).
keyPoints: Concave lens: f = −30 cm; object distance u = −60 cm
Use 1/v = 1/f + 1/u
v = −20 cm — a virtual image, 20 cm from the lens on the object's side

subject: Physics
text: A wire of resistance R is cut into three equal parts. If these three parts are then joined in parallel, calculate the total resistance of the combination so formed. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Each of the three equal parts has resistance R/3 (since resistance is proportional to length, and each part is 1/3 the original length). For three resistors of R/3 each in parallel: 1/Rp = 1/(R/3) + 1/(R/3) + 1/(R/3) = 3/(R/3) = 9/R. So Rp = R/9.
keyPoints: Each of the three equal parts has resistance R/3
For three equal resistors in parallel: 1/Rp = 3/(R/3) = 9/R
Total resistance Rp = R/9

subject: Physics
text: OR: Define electric power. When do we say that the power consumed in an electric circuit is 1 watt? (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed (or work is done) in a circuit: P = W/t = VI. We say the power consumed in a circuit is 1 watt when a current of 1 ampere flows through it under a potential difference of 1 volt (i.e. 1 joule of work is done per second).
keyPoints: Electric power = rate of consumption of electrical energy, P = VI
1 watt = power consumed when 1 A flows under a potential difference of 1 V
Equivalently, 1 watt = 1 joule of energy consumed per second

subject: Biology
text: "Excessive use of chemicals and pesticides in agriculture adversely affect the environment." Justify this statement. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Pesticides and chemical fertilisers, when used excessively, do not fully break down and get washed into soil and water bodies. Being non-biodegradable, they enter the food chain through plants and accumulate in the bodies of organisms at each successive trophic level in increasing concentration (biomagnification) — reaching the highest concentration in top consumers (including humans), causing serious health and ecological harm.
keyPoints: Excess pesticides/chemicals don't fully break down and contaminate soil and water
They enter the food chain through plants
Biomagnification concentrates them further at each trophic level, harming top consumers including humans

subject: Chemistry
text: (a) "Displacement reactions also play a key role in extracting metals in the middle of the reactivity series." Justify this statement with two examples. (b) Why can metals high up in the reactivity series not be obtained by reduction of their oxides by carbon? (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Metals in the middle of the reactivity series can be obtained by displacing them from their compounds using a more reactive element. Examples: (i) ZnO + C → Zn + CO (carbon, acting as a more reactive reducing agent, displaces zinc from zinc oxide); (ii) Fe2O3 + 2Al → 2Fe + Al2O3 (the thermite reaction — aluminium, being more reactive, displaces iron from iron oxide). (b) Metals high up in the reactivity series (like Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot displace/reduce them from their oxides — a less reactive element cannot displace a more reactive one. Such metals are instead obtained by electrolytic reduction of their molten compounds.
keyPoints: Middle-reactivity metals: obtained via displacement by a more reactive reducing agent, e.g. ZnO+C→Zn+CO and the thermite reaction Fe2O3+2Al→2Fe+Al2O3
Top-reactivity metals (Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are more reactive than carbon
Carbon can't displace a more reactive metal from its oxide, so these are extracted by electrolytic reduction of the molten compound instead

subject: Chemistry
text: With the help of an activity, explain the conditions under which iron articles get rusted. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: Take three test tubes with an iron nail in each: Tube 1 has dry air only (with anhydrous calcium chloride to absorb any moisture) — no rusting occurs. Tube 2 has boiled (air-free) distilled water with a layer of oil on top to keep air out — no rusting occurs. Tube 3 has ordinary water exposed to air — the nail rusts. This shows that iron rusts only when both oxygen (air) and moisture (water) are present together; either alone is not enough.
keyPoints: Tube with dry air only (moisture absorbed): no rusting
Tube with air-free boiled water (oil layer keeps air out): no rusting
Tube with water exposed to air: nail rusts — proving both oxygen and moisture are needed together

subject: Chemistry
text: OR: (i) Name two metals which react violently with cold water. List any three observations which a student notes when these metals are dropped in a beaker containing water. (ii) Write a test to identify the gas evolved (if any) during the reaction of these metals with water. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water. Observations: the metal floats and moves rapidly on the water's surface; the reaction is highly exothermic, generating enough heat to melt the metal into a molten globule; a hissing sound is produced, and the evolved hydrogen gas may even catch fire. (ii) Test for the gas: bring a burning matchstick/candle near the gas — it burns with a 'pop' sound, confirming the gas is hydrogen.
keyPoints: Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water
Observations: metal floats and moves rapidly, melts into a molten globule (exothermic), hissing sound, gas may catch fire
Test: a burning matchstick near the gas gives a 'pop' sound, confirming hydrogen

subject: Biology
text: Plants have neither a nervous system nor muscles, even then they respond to stimuli. For example, the leaves of chhui-mui (touch-me-not) plant when touched begin to fold up and droop. (a) How is the information communicated in "touch-me-not" plants? (b) What enables the plant cells to bring out the observable response? (c) Differentiate the movement mentioned above from the movement of tendrils in a pea plant. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Since there is no nervous system, the information (stimulus of touch) is communicated from cell to cell as an electrical/chemical signal that spreads across the plant tissue, without needing specialised nerve cells. (b) A rapid change in the amount of water (turgor pressure) in the cells of the leaf/pulvinus enables them to change shape quickly, producing the observable folding response. (c) The touch-me-not's leaf-folding is a fast movement that does not depend on growth — it results from a quick change in cell water content/turgor. In contrast, a pea plant's tendril movement is a slow, growth-dependent movement — the tendril coils around a support due to differential (faster) growth on the side away from contact, which takes much longer to occur.
keyPoints: Touch-me-not: stimulus communicated cell-to-cell as electrical/chemical signal, with no nervous system involved
Response is enabled by a rapid change in water content/turgor pressure in the cells
Touch-me-not folding is fast and growth-independent; pea tendril coiling is slow and depends on differential growth

subject: Biology
text: (a) What are chromosomes? (b) Explain in brief how stability of DNA content of a species is ensured in sexually reproducing organisms. (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Chromosomes are thread-like structures found in the nucleus of a cell, made of DNA and proteins, which carry the genetic information (genes) passed from parents to offspring. (b) Stability of DNA content is ensured through meiosis: during the formation of gametes (sperm and egg), the chromosome number is halved (diploid → haploid). When two gametes fuse during fertilisation, the normal diploid chromosome number is restored in the offspring — keeping the DNA content constant from one generation to the next.
keyPoints: Chromosomes = thread-like DNA-and-protein structures in the nucleus, carrying genes
Meiosis halves the chromosome number (diploid→haploid) when gametes are formed
Fertilisation (fusion of two gametes) restores the diploid number, keeping DNA content stable across generations

subject: Physics
text: (a) Write the relationship between resistivity and resistance of a cylindrical conductor of length l and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of resistivity. (b) Why are alloys used in electrical heating devices? (2025 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Resistance R = ρl/A, where ρ is the resistivity. Rearranging, ρ = RA/l. Since R is in ohms (Ω), A in square metres (m²) and l in metres (m), the SI unit of resistivity is Ω·m² / m = Ω·m (ohm-metre). (b) Alloys are used in electrical heating devices because they have higher resistivity than pure metals (so they produce more heat for a given current), and they do not oxidise or melt easily even at the high temperatures reached when red hot, making them durable for repeated heating use.
keyPoints: R = ρl/A, so ρ = RA/l
SI unit of resistivity: ohm-metre (Ω·m)
Alloys have higher resistivity (more heating effect) and resist oxidising/melting at high temperatures

subject: Chemistry
text: (i) A compound 'X' which is prepared from gypsum has the property of hardening when mixed with proper quantity of water. Identify 'X' and write its chemical formula. (ii) State the difference in chemical composition between baking soda and baking powder. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) X is Plaster of Paris, CaSO4·½H2O. (ii) Baking soda is a single compound, sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3). Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda with a mild edible acid (such as tartaric acid), so unlike baking soda, it contains an added acid component.
keyPoints: X = Plaster of Paris, CaSO4·½H2O
Baking soda is the single compound NaHCO3
Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda plus a mild acid (e.g. tartaric acid)

subject: Chemistry
text: OR: Write balanced chemical equation for the reaction that occurs when: (i) blue coloured copper sulphate crystals are heated and (ii) sodium hydrogen carbonate is heated during cooking. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) CuSO4·5H2O --(heat)--> CuSO4 + 5H2O (blue hydrated copper sulphate turns white anhydrous copper sulphate as water of crystallisation is driven off). (ii) 2NaHCO3 --(heat)--> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2 (sodium hydrogen carbonate decomposes on heating to sodium carbonate, water and carbon dioxide).
keyPoints: CuSO4·5H2O (blue) → CuSO4 (white) + 5H2O on heating
2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2 on heating
Both are thermal decomposition reactions

subject: Biology
text: (a) Write the role of insulin in regulating blood sugar levels in human body. Mention the disease caused due to it. (b) How is the timing and the amount of release of insulin in the blood regulated? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Insulin lowers blood sugar by promoting the uptake of glucose into cells and its conversion into glycogen for storage; insufficient insulin secretion or its improper action causes diabetes (high blood sugar). (b) The timing and amount of insulin release is regulated by a feedback mechanism: the pancreas (beta cells of the islets of Langerhans) monitors blood glucose levels and secretes insulin in response to rising sugar levels; as blood sugar returns to normal, insulin secretion decreases.
keyPoints: Insulin lowers blood sugar by promoting glucose uptake/storage as glycogen
Insufficient insulin causes diabetes
Release is regulated by feedback: pancreas senses blood sugar level and adjusts insulin secretion accordingly

subject: Biology
text: Name the type of blood (oxygenated/deoxygenated) transported by each of the following, mentioning the path (i.e. from one organ to another): (i) Vena cava (ii) Pulmonary artery. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from the body tissues to the right atrium of the heart. (ii) Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs.
keyPoints: Vena cava: deoxygenated blood, from body tissues to the right atrium
Pulmonary artery: deoxygenated blood, from the right ventricle to the lungs
Both carry deoxygenated blood despite one being called an 'artery'

subject: Biology
text: OR: With the help of a schematic flow chart, show the breakdown of glucose in a cell to provide energy (i) in the presence of oxygen (ii) in lack of oxygen. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Glucose is first broken down to pyruvate (glycolysis, in the cytoplasm) in all cases. (i) In the presence of oxygen: pyruvate enters the mitochondria and is completely broken down to CO2 and water, releasing a large amount of energy (aerobic respiration). (ii) In the lack of oxygen: pyruvate is converted either to lactic acid (in muscle cells, causing cramps) or to ethanol and CO2 (in yeast, during fermentation), releasing much less energy (anaerobic respiration).
keyPoints: Glucose → pyruvate (glycolysis) happens first in all cases
With oxygen: pyruvate → CO2 + water in mitochondria, releasing more energy
Without oxygen: pyruvate → lactic acid (muscles) or ethanol + CO2 (yeast), releasing less energy

subject: Biology
text: Name the part of the human excretory system where nephrons are found. Write the structure and function of nephrons. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Nephrons are found in the kidneys. Structure: each nephron has a cup-shaped Bowman's capsule surrounding a cluster of blood capillaries (the glomerulus), connected to a long, coiled tubule. Function: the glomerulus/Bowman's capsule filters the blood, and as the filtrate passes along the tubule, useful substances (glucose, amino acids, some water and salts) are selectively reabsorbed back into the blood, while the remaining filtrate becomes urine.
keyPoints: Nephrons are found in the kidneys
Structure: Bowman's capsule (surrounding the glomerulus) connected to a long tubule
Function: filters blood, then selectively reabsorbs useful substances, leaving urine

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: OR: It is observed that the power of an eye to see nearby objects as well as far off objects diminishes with age. (i) Give reason for the above statement. (ii) Name the defect that is likely to arise in the eyes in such a condition. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) With age, the ciliary muscles of the eye weaken and the eye lens loses its elasticity, so it can no longer adjust its curvature/focal length properly to focus on both near and distant objects. (ii) This defect is called presbyopia.
keyPoints: Ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens loses elasticity with age
The lens can no longer adjust focal length properly for near or far objects
This age-related defect is called presbyopia

subject: Biology
text: How do harmful chemicals get accumulated progressively at each trophic level in a food chain? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: Harmful chemicals (like pesticides) enter the food chain through producers, which absorb them from the soil or water. Since these chemicals are non-biodegradable, they are not excreted and instead accumulate in the bodies of organisms; at each successive trophic level, the concentration increases further because each consumer eats many organisms from the level below, concentrating their accumulated chemicals. This progressive increase up the food chain is called biological magnification (biomagnification), and it reaches its highest concentration in the top consumers.
keyPoints: Chemicals enter the food chain via producers absorbing them from soil/water
Being non-biodegradable, they accumulate in bodies rather than being excreted
Concentration increases at each trophic level (biomagnification), highest in top consumers

subject: Chemistry
text: (a) Identify the reducing agent in the following reactions: (i) 4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O (ii) H2O + F2 → HF + HOF (iii) Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2 (iv) 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. (b) Define a redox reaction in terms of gain or loss of oxygen. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) (i) NH3 is the reducing agent (nitrogen is oxidised). (ii) H2O is the reducing agent (oxygen is oxidised, going from −2 in H2O towards 0 in HOF). (iii) CO is the reducing agent (it is oxidised to CO2, while Fe2O3 is reduced to Fe). (iv) H2 is the reducing agent (it is oxidised by combining with oxygen). (b) A redox reaction, in terms of oxygen, is one in which oxidation (gain of oxygen by one reactant) and reduction (loss of oxygen by another reactant) occur simultaneously.
keyPoints: Reducing agents: (i) NH3 (ii) H2O (iii) CO (iv) H2 — each is the substance that gets oxidised
A reducing agent is the substance that is itself oxidised in the reaction
Redox reaction = simultaneous oxidation (gain of oxygen) and reduction (loss of oxygen)

subject: Chemistry
text: (a) Suggest one remedial measure each to counteract the change in pH in human beings in the following cases: (i) Production of too much acid in stomach during indigestion (ii) Stung by a honey bee/nettle leaves. (b) Fresh milk has a pH of 6. When it changes into curd will its pH increase or decrease? Why? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) (i) Take a mild base/antacid (like milk of magnesia, containing magnesium hydroxide) to neutralise the excess stomach acid. (ii) Apply a mild base (like baking soda solution) to neutralise the acidic sting and relieve the irritation. (b) The pH decreases (curd becomes more acidic than milk) because lactic acid bacteria ferment the lactose in milk into lactic acid, increasing its acidity.
keyPoints: Indigestion: take an antacid (mild base like milk of magnesia) to neutralise excess acid
Bee sting/nettle sting: apply a mild base like baking soda solution
Milk → curd: pH decreases, because lactic acid bacteria ferment lactose into lactic acid

subject: Biology
text: (i) State the role of ATP in cellular respiration. (ii) What ensures sufficient exchange of gases in plants? (iii) State the conditions on which the direction of diffusion of gases in a plant depend upon. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) ATP is the energy currency of the cell — energy released during the breakdown of glucose in respiration is stored in ATP molecules, which is then used to power the cell's energy-requiring activities. (ii) Stomata (numerous pores on the leaf surface, providing a large combined surface area) ensure sufficient gas exchange in plants. (iii) The direction of gas diffusion depends on the plant's environmental conditions and metabolic needs at that time — e.g. in bright light, photosynthesis dominates (CO2 diffuses in, O2 diffuses out); in the dark, respiration dominates (O2 diffuses in, CO2 diffuses out) — i.e. it depends on the relative rates of respiration and photosynthesis at that time.
keyPoints: ATP stores the energy released during respiration, for the cell to use later
Stomata (large combined surface area) ensure sufficient gas exchange
Diffusion direction depends on whether photosynthesis or respiration dominates at that time

subject: Biology
text: OR: (i) What is the internal energy reserve in plants and animals? (ii) How do desert plants perform photosynthesis if their stomata remain closed during the day? (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) The internal energy reserve is starch in plants and glycogen in animals. (ii) Desert plants keep their stomata closed during the day to minimise water loss through transpiration; they open their stomata at night to take in and store CO2 (as organic acids), which is then used internally for photosynthesis during the day even with the stomata closed.
keyPoints: Energy reserve: starch in plants, glycogen in animals
Desert plants keep stomata closed by day to reduce water loss
They take in and store CO2 at night, using it internally for daytime photosynthesis

chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
subject: Physics
text: Give reasons for the following: (a) Danger signals installed at airports and at the top of tall buildings are of red colour. (b) The sky appears dark to the passengers flying at very high altitudes. (c) The path of a beam of light passing through a colloidal solution is visible. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (a) Red light is scattered/deviated the least among visible colours (due to its longer wavelength), so it travels the longest distance through air without being scattered away, making it visible from far off — ideal for a warning signal. (b) At high altitudes the atmosphere is very thin/rarefied, so there is very little air/dust to scatter sunlight; with little scattered light reaching the eye, the sky appears dark rather than blue. (c) This is the Tyndall effect — colloidal particles suspended in the solution scatter the light passing through it, making the beam's path visible.
keyPoints: Red light scatters the least, so it travels farthest — good for warning signals
At high altitude, thin air scatters very little sunlight, so the sky looks dark
Visible beam path through a colloidal solution = the Tyndall effect (light scattering by suspended particles)

subject: Physics
text: (i) State the rule used to find the force acting on a current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. (ii) Given three cases of an electron entering a magnetic field: (i) velocity perpendicular to the field, (ii) velocity at an angle to the field, (iii) velocity parallel to the field (same direction as the field). Identify the case in which the force will be maximum and minimum respectively. Give reason for your answer. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule is used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. (ii) The force F = qvB sinθ, where θ is the angle between the velocity and the field. It is maximum when the velocity is perpendicular to the field (θ=90°, sinθ=1) — case (i); and minimum (zero) when the velocity is parallel to the field (θ=0°, sinθ=0) — case (iii). Case (ii), with an intermediate angle, gives an intermediate force value.
keyPoints: Rule: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
Force F = qvB sinθ depends on the angle θ between velocity and field
Maximum force when velocity ⊥ field (case i); minimum (zero) when velocity ∥ field (case iii)

subject: Biology
text: (i) Why does a kitchen garden called an artificial ecosystem while a forest is considered to be a natural ecosystem? (ii) While designing an artificial ecosystem at home, write any two things to be kept in mind to convert it into a self-sustaining system. Give reason to justify your answer. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) A kitchen garden is an artificial ecosystem because it is created and maintained through human intervention (planting, watering, fertilising); a forest is natural because it develops and sustains itself without any human effort. (ii) Two things to keep in mind: include decomposers, so that dead plant matter is broken down and nutrients are recycled back into the soil; and maintain a balanced mix of producers and consumers, so the food chain/energy flow can sustain itself. Without these, nutrients would not cycle and the system would keep needing external inputs rather than sustaining itself.
keyPoints: Kitchen garden needs human intervention (artificial); forest sustains itself without human effort (natural)
Include decomposers, so nutrients get recycled back into the soil
Maintain a balanced producer-consumer ratio, so the food chain can sustain itself

subject: Biology
text: OR: (i) Construct a food chain of four trophic levels comprising the following: Hawk, snake, plants, rat. (ii) 20,000 J of energy was transferred by the producers to the organism of second trophic level. Calculate the amount of energy that will be transferred by organisms of the third trophic level to the organisms of the fourth trophic level. (2023 Board)
modelAnswer: (i) Food chain: Plants → Rat → Snake → Hawk. (ii) Only about 10% of energy is transferred between successive trophic levels. From the 2nd trophic level (rat, 20,000 J) to the 3rd (snake): 10% of 20,000 = 2,000 J. From the 3rd (snake) to the 4th (hawk): 10% of 2,000 = 200 J. So the energy transferred from the third to the fourth trophic level is 200 J.
keyPoints: Food chain: Plants → Rat → Snake → Hawk
Only ~10% of energy passes to the next trophic level
3rd level receives 2,000 J (10% of 20,000); 4th level receives 200 J (10% of 2,000)
